definition: Parity problems are widely used as benchmark problems in genetic programming but inherited from the artificial neural network community.
details: Parity is calculated by summing all the binary inputs and reporting if the sum is odd or even. This is considered difficult because: a very simple artificial neural network cannot solve it, and all inputs need to be considered and a change to any one of them changes the answer.

explainer.lead: The parity problem is a standard benchmark in genetic programming, taken from the artificial neural network community. It is hard because every input must be considered and flipping any one bit flips the answer.

tiers.eli5: You add up a row of ones and zeroes and say whether the total is odd or even; changing one number changes the verdict.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use parity to test whether an evolved or learned program captures an all-inputs interaction. The pitfall is that a very simple neural network cannot solve it, so poor results may reflect model capacity rather than the method.
tiers.paperLevel: Parity is computed by summing all binary inputs and reporting whether the sum is odd or even. Its difficulty is that no single input matters alone: all inputs must be considered, and a change to any one of them changes the answer.

explainer.example: With inputs 1, 0, 1 the sum is 2, so the parity output is even; changing the middle bit to 1 gives 3 and flips the output to odd.
